## BUG-050

**Command / Area:** Beam label placement — all beam commands (1, 2, 4, 5, 8 etc.) that call `BeamTextPlacementService.TryPlaceBeamLabel`.

**Symptom:** If you draw a beam from LEFT to RIGHT and run the label command, the label lands on one physical side (e.g. below). If you draw the SAME beam from RIGHT to LEFT (reversed endpoints), the label lands on a DIFFERENT physical side or at a different offset distance — even though the geometry is identical. The label position changes depending on which end you clicked first when drawing the beam.

**Expected behaviour:** The label should always land on the same physical side at the same perpendicular distance regardless of which endpoint is pt1 and which is pt2.

**Root cause:** `TryPlaceBeamLabel` computes `preferredSide` from the xref-vote (negCount vs posCount), where the signed distance of an xref wall changes sign when the beam direction is reversed. A wall that gives `negCount=1` for a forward beam gives `posCount=1` for the reversed beam. This flips `preferredSide`, but the `FinalOffset` formula then picks a different xrefBase (`furthestPosDist` vs `furthestNegDist`) that yields a different physical offset — so both the side AND the magnitude change. `SelectSideBaseDistance` was designed for a fixed-direction perpAngle convention (J16), but that convention breaks when pt1/pt2 are swapped.

**Reference:** `CE_STRUC_SUITE/Services/BeamTextPlacementService.cs` — `TryPlaceBeamLabel`, `FinalOffset` closure, `SelectSideBaseDistance`. Confirmed by headless test S8 (2026-06-09).

**Evidence from S8:**
- Forward beam (0,0)→(5000,0) with wall at Y=+200: label lands at Y=-400 (perpDist=400, below beam). ✓
- Reversed beam (5000,0)→(0,0) with identical wall: label lands at Y=0 (perpDist=0, ON beam). ✗
- diff=400 drawing units.

**Fix:** Added `CanonicalizeBeamDirection(pt1, pt2)` to `BeamTextPlacementService` and called it at the very start of `TryPlaceBeamLabel` (before computing `beamDir`, `mid`, `angles`). The helper ensures the beam always runs left-to-right (horizontal) or bottom-to-top (vertical) so `perpAngle` and `SignedDistanceToBeam` produce consistent physical-side signs regardless of draw direction. `angles` is recomputed from canonical points. Confirmed by headless rig: S8 now passes (23/23 PASS, 0 fail). Files changed: `CE_STRUC_SUITE/Services/BeamTextPlacementService.cs`.

**Status:** FIXED 2026-06-09 — awaiting Tim's AutoCAD confirmation.

## BUG-052

**Command / Area:** PIT BLOCK 3 — force-adoption + elimination of PIT BLOCK 2 across the suite. PIT/IO/OF/etc. inserts, drawing-open behaviour, installer payload.

**Symptom (Tim, 2026-06-12):** "Why are we on v2.1.3 and still not force-using PIT BLOCK 3? Why hasn't it shipped? How does it get rid of all use of PIT BLOCK 2?"

**Root cause found:**
1. **PIT BLOCK 3.dwg was never in the running bundle.** `DeployToDevBundle` (the dev workflow) copies only the DLL/assets/icons/runtimes — NOT block `.dwg` files. Blocks ship only via the installer EXE, and no EXE has been built since PB3 was added to `source_blocks` on 9 Jun. The bundle's `Contents\Blocks\` was frozen at an old install (only `PIT BLOCK 2.dwg`, dated 4 Feb). So the code's "prefer PB3" preference could never find the file → silently fell back to PB2.
2. **Current design is PREFERENCE, not FORCE.** New pits prefer PB3; old drawings keep PB2/PB until someone manually runs `CDREFRESHBLOCKS`. Nothing auto-forces.
3. **PB2 is deliberately KEPT** (recognised, 2nd variant, shipped) — by design it coexists, it does not get eliminated.

**Tim's decisions (2026-06-12):** FULL FORCE + ELIMINATE PB2; deliver via FULL INSTALLER EXE for the office.

**DONE this session (safe, immediate):**
- `DeployToDevBundle` now syncs `Installer\source_blocks\*.dwg` → bundle `Contents\Blocks` every dev build (root-cause fix so blocks never go missing again).
- Copied `PIT BLOCK 3.dwg` into the running bundle NOW → new pits resolve PB3 immediately (Tim can verify: place a pit → Properties reads "PIT BLOCK 3").

**REMAINING (force + eliminate) — gated on AC-closed + Tim's one real-drawing test before office EXE:**
- **Auto-redefine on drawing open:** wire the `CDREFRESHBLOCKS` redefine (`db.Insert(name, PB3sourceDb, true)`) to run once-per-database on open/first-CE-touch (reuse the hardened once-per-db `EnsureDrawingDiscovered` hook + CommandInProgress guard — DO NOT add a new DocumentActivated reactor; this is the recurring-regression zone, see memory regression_dbtext_dtext_doubleclick). Redefines in-drawing PB/PB2 defs from PB3.dwg → all existing pits show PB3 geometry automatically.
- **Eliminate the PB2 NAME (destructive):** reassign every pit BlockReference from "PIT BLOCK 2"/"PIT BLOCK" to the "PIT BLOCK 3" definition (preserve dynamic props: SPS_RADIUS, X/Y width, visibility states), then purge the PB2/PB defs so Properties reads "PIT BLOCK 3" everywhere. PRECONDITION: verify PB2↔PB3 dynamic-property names are identical (PB3 was built from PB2 — likely safe, but MUST confirm or pits break — the 2026-06-09 note warned of exactly this). Drop PB2 from `GetBlockNameVariants`, remove `PIT BLOCK 2.dwg` from `source_blocks`, keep recognition ONLY for the in-session migration pass.
- **Verify:** unit tests (variant order now `["PIT BLOCK 3","PIT BLOCK"]`; every-recognition-site test) + headless redefine/reassign round-trip (isolated accoreconsole, runs with AC open).
- **Ship:** close AC → build net48+net10 (DLL now carries blocks) → bump 2.1.4 → build installer EXE → Tim test: open an OLD PB2 job → all pits read "PIT BLOCK 3", SPS grip works, PITSCHEDULE/CDEDIT fine, nothing lost → THEN distribute EXE.

**Update 2026-06-12 (code complete, headless-proven):** `PitBlockMigrationService` built (pure
planner + apply + auto-on-open trigger + CDREFRESHBLOCKS wiring). PB2↔PB3 confirmed structurally
identical (15 ents, 0 attrs) so redefine + RENAME (handle-preserving) is safe — no reference swap,
CE link graph intact. Tests: 8 planner + 3 wiring + headless T3 (7/7 incl. handle preserved, name→PB3,
still recognised). Full suite 1918/1944. Residual v1 limits: mixed PB2+PB3 drawings keep a few PB2
names (geometry uniform); PB2.dwg still shipped/recognised for un-migrated drawings (final cleanup
gated on rollout). REMAINING: Tim closes AC → deploy v2.1.4 (DLL now carries blocks) → build office
EXE → Tim runs the 5-step AC test in REGRESSION_LOG → distribute.

**Status:** IN PROGRESS — code + tests + headless DONE 2026-06-12; gated on AC-closed deploy + Tim's real-drawing test before office EXE.

## BUG-101

**Command / Area:** CDSTRIP Accept (atomic read-back of the fall-arrow Leaders); vertex prompt wording; preview wording.

**Symptom:** typed `A` at the preview → `[CE] A staged fall arrow differs from the accepted plan.` — nothing drawn. `Next point [Undo] [Undo]`. `Preview: … Zero justification` after choosing Center.

**Root cause:** AutoCAD hides a Leader arrowhead when the shaft is shorter than 2 × Dimasz × Dimscale (= 600 mm for TIM LEADER); the shaft was exactly 600 and rounds to 599.999… in most directions (measured in accoreconsole 2027: 599 no head, 600/601 head). The atomic read-back saw `HasArrowHead == false` and refused. The old route drew those arrows headless silently.

**Status:** FIXED IN SOURCE — 2026-09-14 (REGRESSION_LOG BUG-101): shaft 610 mm, every-degree guard test, prompt/wording fixes, specific read-back message. Awaiting Tim's AutoCAD retest.

## BUG-489

**Command / Area:** AUDIT 01 A2 + A3 (privacy, near-blocker): the CESUPPORT zip cleaner misses drawing names that have no ".dwg", and lets folder paths and PDF paths through. The cleaner (Modules/Manager/Services/CeSupportBundleScrub.cs 19-35) only cuts paths and bare names that end in a drawing type (dwg, dxf, dwt, dws, dwl, dwf, bak). Lines that escape (A2): Modules/Drainage/Core/JobTime/JobTimeTracker.cs 155, 216, 323, 345 log session.DrawingName, the name with no extension (JobTimeSession.cs 151); Modules/Drainage/Services/ProjectDataService.Mutations.cs 124, 181, 197, 261 and ProjectDataService.KeptRecords.cs 140, 143 log the project file path, which is CD_ProjectData_<drawing name>_<hash>.json (ProjectDataService.Persistence.cs 1339-1343); the user-folder part becomes %USERPROFILE% but the drawing name stays. Triggered by opening, switching to or leaving idle any drawing, then CESUPPORT: every zip from the last 14 days of logs lists the drawings the colleague worked on. Lines that escape (A3): Services/StormReportReader.cs 349 (rating-report PDF path in the job folder, on a read failure); Commands/LinkCommands.ImportXcivil.Corpus.cs 422, 486, 546 (configured / PDF paths, Debug lines, always written); Services/DrawingBackupService.cs 355 (backup folder named after the drawing, 333-337, on a listing failure). What leaks: everything in the path after the user folder (OneDrive folder, project folder, job folder name; job folders can hold a street name). This corrects the hunt/W45 belief that the zip is fully scrubbed (it is clean for login, PC name and names ending in a drawing type only). Right result: log the job number (or a short code) instead of DrawingName and the project file path; add a cleaner rule that cuts CD_ProjectData_<...>.json names; and treat any drive or server path (any extension, or a folder) like a drawing path, keeping only the job number. To SEE: open two drawings, switch between them, run CESUPPORT, then search every file in the zip for the drawing names and for "STORM" or ".pdf" paths. ## BUG-495

**Command / Area:** COLLEAGUE RELEASE GATE CANDIDATE. HUNT2-S-01 (HIGH): Publish Issue (CESHEETS > Publish Issue, and the Sheets Manager window) gives the typed revision and the issue date to EVERY Structural sheet in the job, including sheets the drafter left out of this issue. What the drafter sees: a 10-sheet set where only S03 and S05 changed comes out with all ten at revision C, dated today. Eight sheets that did not change now claim a change; a builder holding revision B of S07 is told it is superseded when it is not. Sheets left out of the issue also jump to C in the sheet list without ever being issued. Evidence (reading only): UI/Dialogs/CeSheetsWindow.xaml.cs 263-273 (called at 492) writes the revision onto every Structural sheet; SheetsOfDiscipline 206-212 ignores the tick 'include in issue'; Services/CeSheetsIssueService.cs 24-32 and 86-109 date every sheet when no ticked list is given; CeSheetsManagerWindow.xaml.cs 1191-1196 does the same. The Publish Issue window also refuses a blank revision (CeIssuePublishDialog.xaml.cs 198-200) against INT-059 item 22. It breaks Tim's 14 Sep ruling (card 04_REFERENCE/structural/cards/STRUC-REGISTER-ISSUE_CARD_2026-09-26.md section 4): 'Unchanged sheets keep their existing revision and date, a set-wide issue date must never overwrite them' and 'Before plotting, show an issue preview'. Right result: only the ticked sheets get the new revision and date, and the issue preview is shown before anything plots. Wrong: sheets 1 and 2 at C dated today and sheet 3 also at C in the list. Right: sheet 3 stays at B. ## BUG-505

**Command / Area:** COLLEAGUE RELEASE GATE CANDIDATE. HUNT2-C-01 (HIGH): the X-Civil and LandXML imports never read the source drawing's UNITS, so a millimetre job can come in 1000 times too big, silently. What the drafter sees: CDIMPORTXCIVIL on a millimetre X-Civil drawing puts the pits and pipes 1000 times further from the origin than the X-Civil linework, and 1000 times too big, with no line on the command line saying CE changed the scale. The same happens for any X-Civil or LandXML import into a drawing whose UNITS are Metres. A wrong scale on a whole job is the risk: every pit position and size on the drawing is wrong, and nothing warns the drafter. Evidence (reading only): Services/XcivilEntityScanner.cs 427-486 guesses whether the X-Civil drawing is in metres and stops at the FIRST thing that looks metre-sized (one pit block 0.05 to 3.0 wide, 436-442, or one polyline on a pipe layer 1 to 250 long, 448-455), although the comment says 'if EVERY named pit'. Then every position, pit size and pipe diameter is multiplied by 1000 (499-518, called at Services/XcivilImportService.cs 323-325); the scale goes only to the debug file (324). Neither this route nor the LandXML route (Helpers/LandXmlParser.cs 170-173) looks at the CURRENT drawing's UNITS: both always place in millimetres. The downpipe symbol reader does use the drawing's UNITS (Services/BackgroundDownpipeSymbolReader.cs 73-77). I think a 200 mm stub, a short leader or a short tail of pipe linework on a pipe layer is common in a millimetre drawing, so a real job can trip this. Right result: CE reads the X-Civil drawing's UNITS and the target drawing's UNITS, scales between them, and says so in one line ('X-Civil drawing is in metres; placed in this millimetre drawing at 1000 times'); where the units are not set it asks once. Smallest fix: use both drawings' Insunits (the same DrawingAreaUnits.MillimetresPerUnit the downpipe reader uses); keep the guess only when UNITS are not set, require most pits to agree, and print the scale used. No test today for the scale guess. To SEE it: take a COPY of a millimetre X-Civil drawing that imports correctly today, add one 200 mm polyline on its pipe layer, save; CDIMPORTXCIVIL into a copy of a job drawing; ZOOM Extents. Wrong: everything 1000 times out. Then set UNITS to Metres in a copy of the target drawing and import again. Right: a one-line scale message and the job in the right place. ## BUG-506

**Command / Area:** HUNT2-C-02 (MEDIUM): the CDDESIGN calculation summary prints the connection pipe grade as '1:0'. What the reviewer sees: under CONNECTION PIPE the summary reads 'Diameter 100 mm' and 'Grade 1:0' for any grade flatter than 1 in 2. A wrong number on a design sheet is the risk: a reviewer cannot read the grade, and a report with '1:0' on it cannot be issued. Evidence (reading only): the pipe sizer hands back the grade as N in '1 in N', for example 100 (Services/PipeSizingSolver.cs 235; CDDESIGN keeps it as connectionGradeN, Services/AutoDesignService.cs 113-114 and 648-651). The summary treats it as a slope and divides 1 by it, giving 0.01, rounded to 0, printed '1:0' (Services/DesignProposalReport.cs 280-284). The test Modules/Drainage.Tests/Services/DesignProposalReportTests.cs line 55 feeds the summary 0.01, which the real design never produces, so the test passes and the screen is wrong; DetailSelectorTests.cs 718 feeds 100.0, the real form. Right result: 'Grade 1:100' (the N the sizer gave). Smallest fix: print '1:' + N without dividing, and change the report test to feed 100. To SEE it: a copy of a job with a council and areas set; CDDESIGN, work the design out, read CONNECTION PIPE in the summary. Wrong: Grade 1:0. Right: Grade 1:100. **Command / Area:** HUNT2-C-03 (MEDIUM, breaks R-12 'Unknown stays Unknown'): CDCALC's Boyd's tab opens with another job's figures, and they flow on to the Detention tab and to CDDESIGN. Right result: empty boxes that say 'Unknown, not entered', no storage worked out and nothing offered to the Detention tab until real figures are typed. To SEE it: a copy of a job that has never had CDCALC saved; CDCALC, open Boyd's, read the boxes; open the Detention tab and read the suggested volume; save, close, run CDDESIGN and read the site area. ## BUG-508

**Command / Area:** HUNT2-C-04 (MEDIUM): CDDESIGN works the flows and the connection pipe off the office rainfall curve, even when the job has its own curve, and says nothing. What the reviewer sees: a job with its own rainfall coefficients (CDRAINFALL). The storage and the permitted discharge use the job's curve, but 'Q minor', 'Q major' and the connection pipe size in the summary come from the office Melbourne curve. A wrong number on a design is the risk: two halves of one design on different rainfall with no word. DAY1 notes the office curve reads 6.5 to 8.6 per cent high against a real issued sheet. Evidence (reading only): the flows come from RationalFlowService.ComputeMinorMajorWithNotes (Services/AutoDesignService.cs 101-114), which calls ComputeFlow and GetIntensity, and GetIntensity always uses the office curve (Services/RationalFlowService.cs 199-200, 264-288, 330-353); the job's curve is never passed in. The storage and permitted discharge do use it (Services/DetentionSizingService.cs 129-133 and 270-273; Services/AutoDesignService.cs 389-392, whose own comment says both halves must be on the same rainfall). Right result: all flows on the job's curve, or a line saying which curve each figure used. Smallest fix: pass the job's curve into ComputeMinorMajorWithNotes and ComputeFlow and use RainfallCurves.CurveInUse(curve) there like the storage does. No test gives the flows a job curve. To SEE it: a copy of a job; CDRAINFALL, set the job's own coefficients; CDDESIGN, read Q minor and Q major; compare with the same figures worked by hand from the job's curve. Wrong: they match the office curve. Right: they match the job's curve. **Command / Area:** HUNT2-C-08 (MEDIUM, breaks R-12 'Unknown stays Unknown'): LandXML import fills in a 375 mm pipe, a 600 x 600 pit and STORMPRO SN12 when the file says nothing, and marks them 'from the file'. What the drafter sees: CDIMPORTLANDXML on a file where a pipe has no size, a structure has no size, or a pipe has no material. The pipe is drawn and labelled 375 DIA, the pit 600 x 600, the material STORMPRO SN12, with no line saying these were not in the file. A wrong number on a design is the risk: an invented pipe size looks exactly like a surveyed one, and later steps (capacity, cover, CDRULES) calculate from it. Evidence (reading only): Helpers/LandXmlParser.cs 313 ('reasonable default' 375), 195-196 (600 x 600), 416-417 (STORMPRO SN12). The pipe is then marked as having a real size from the file (HasExplicitDiameter = true, DiameterSource = 'LandXML', 329-331), so later steps cannot tell it was invented. The X-Civil route marks the same case 'default' and 'uncertain' (Services/XcivilEntityScanner.Pipes.cs 1132-1136). Modules/Drainage.Tests/Helpers/LandXmlParserTests.cs covers missing positions (CL1), not missing sizes or material. Right result: size and material stay Unknown, shown as 'SIZE NOT IN FILE', and one line lists each one. Smallest fix: leave the size at 0 with HasExplicitDiameter = false and DiameterSource = 'default' like X-Civil, and list the gaps in the import report. To SEE it: copy a LandXML file and delete one pipe's CircPipe element and one structure's RectStruct; CDIMPORTLANDXML into a copy of a drawing; read the pipe label, the pit size and the command line. Wrong: 375 DIA and 600 x 600 with no warning. Right: SIZE NOT IN FILE and a list. **Command / Area:** HUNT3 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4 (4.3 MEDIUM because the command is live; the rest LOW-MEDIUM; breaks the Settings-first rule R-00): new engineering values have no row on the Settings window, so a drafter cannot see or change them; and the three lintel tolerances have no per-job layer. What the drafter sees: (a) Civil, the speed in a pipe leaving a pit (1.5 m/s recommended, 2.0 m/s limit, AS/NZS 3500.3 5.4.11.2(d)): no row on Settings; only CDRULES prints the figures. (b) Civil, the flattest detention pipe (1 in 200 from 225 mm up): no row. (c) Structural, the footing width FADOPT offers when the width is unknown (300 mm strip, 300 mm beam, 150 mm screw pile): no row and no plain label; any start-up or recovery line names it by splitting the code name ('Footing width: strip width mm'). (d) Structural lintel proposal and framing legend values: no row, no label (those commands are OFF today); the lintel tolerances (smallest opening 600 mm, offset 150 mm, two-face 350 mm, 2 degrees) are office-only, but Tim said lintel tolerances are 'different depending on the job' (INT-075 Set A 8, desk reading: office default plus a job override), and no job override exists; and the framing legend layer colour defaults to 7 (white), which sits badly with INT-077 item 1 ('never white or colour 7'). ## BUG-521

**Command / Area:** HUNT3 5.1 (MEDIUM, ENGINEERING-RESULT RISK): the minimum pipe cover is read from two places that can disagree on the same pit. CDRULES uses council, then project, then office; the CE Inspector (network summary and pit cover row) and the Design Check Dashboard and repair checks use the office value only. A wrong answer on a design check is the risk: the same pit can pass in the Inspector and be a warning in CDRULES, or the other way round, and a drafter who trusts the Inspector can issue a pipe that is too shallow for the council. Example: a council job with a 450 mm council minimum and the office 300 mm: a pit with 350 mm cover is OK in the Inspector and a warning in CDRULES. The in-code fall-back is also 600 mm while the Settings default is 300 mm, so a blank value gives a third answer. Same kind as BUG-255 (Edit Pipe size strip uses a fixed 600 mm cover), in other places. Evidence (reading only): CDRULES Modules/Drainage/Rules/RulebookValues.cs 210-220 (council > project > office); Services/InspectorPaletteService.cs 2335 and 3036, Services/LinkService.RepairAudit.Analysis.cs 191 and 251 all read DesignStandards.MinimumCoverDepth and fall back to 600 mm; Settings default 300 mm at Models/UserSettings.cs 1174. No test covers the three sources together. Right result: every place that judges cover asks the same reader and gets the council value first. Smallest fix: make the four places read the resolved rulebook value (the BUG-255 cure applied here too). To SEE it: on a copy, give a job a council minimum cover of 450 mm and the office 300 mm; put a pit at 350 mm cover; read the Inspector, the Design Check Dashboard and CDRULES. Wrong: Inspector OK, CDRULES warning. Right: all three say warning at 450 mm. Related: the pipe speed limit has the same split (BUG-527). Source file: C:\CE_PLAN\areas\release-v3-colleagues-HUNT3_CROSS_2026-10-09.md (cross-cutting bug hunt 3, 9 Oct; Civil read at 319ba688; nothing built or run; none seen in AutoCAD).

## BUG-522

**Command / Area:** HUNT3 6.1 (LOW): nothing at start-up notices two different copies of CE_SHARED. Civil and Manager must ship byte-identical CE_SHARED because AutoCAD loads whichever copy comes first and the other plugin silently uses it. What could happen: a PC with a half-finished update (see BUG-478) has Civil from one release and Manager from another; AutoCAD uses the first loaded copy and nothing says so, so a button or window can behave as the older release. The hunt checked today's installed bundles and they are clean (byte-identical CE_SHARED.dll in all three lanes, all dated 9 Oct 08:35-08:36), so this is a guard that is missing, not a fault on Tim's PC today. Evidence (reading only): Shared/CE_SHARED/CE_SHARED.csproj 15 gives AssemblyVersion 1.1.0.0, fixed, so the version number never tells two copies apart; no start-up check in Civil or Manager compares the CE_SHARED AutoCAD actually loaded with the one in the plugin's own bundle. A Manager release build does refuse a CE_SHARED that is not the approved Civil one (Modules/Manager/CE_SUITE_MANAGER.csproj 175-216, pair approval at Services/CeApprovedReleaseService.cs 136), but that guard does not run on a colleague's PC. Right result: Civil and Manager compare the loaded file with their own copy at start and print one plain line if they differ. Smallest fix: 'CE Civil and CE Manager are from different releases: run the CE installer again.' To SEE it: on a copy of a bundle, swap Manager's CE_SHARED.dll for an older one and start AutoCAD. Wrong: silence. Right: the line. Source file: C:\CE_PLAN\areas\release-v3-colleagues-HUNT3_CROSS_2026-10-09.md (cross-cutting bug hunt 3, 9 Oct; nothing built or run; none seen in AutoCAD).

## BUG-532

**Command / Area:** R00_STRUC items 28 and 29 (MEDIUM; layer names written into the code, and four objects drawn on two different layer names). What the drafter sees: the same kind of object lands on a different layer depending on which command drew it, so a footing plan's layers split between commands and drafters. The four cases: (1) bored piers: BP uses 'BORED PIER' (Modules/Structural/Services/FoundationService.cs 2013) but the layer map, the native pier tool and the bored pier plan use 'BORED PIER UNDER' (Services/LayerService.cs 94, Services/NativeBoredPierService.cs 14, Models/UserSettings.cs 1583). (2) joists: 'JOISTS' (Commands/RafterJoistCommands.cs 21) against 'FLOOR JOISTS' (Models/UserSettings.cs 1257). (3) stump footings: 'STUMP FOOTING' (Services/FoundationStumpFootingService.cs 14) against 'BORED PIER UNDER' in the layer map (Services/LayerService.cs 97). (4) pads and strips both go on 'STRIP FOOTINGS' (Services/LayerService.cs 95-96). Behind it: Services/LayerService.cs 87-118 maps each kind of object to a layer name written in the code (BEAM, BEAM LOWER, LOADBEARING WALL, WALL BRACING TYPE A and B, SUPPORT COLUMN, SUPPORT DS, BORED PIER UNDER, STRIP FOOTINGS, SLAB INTERNAL BEAM, 35CONT, 25DIMS, 25TEXT, BATTER, GUIDELINES and the rest), and there are 63 more named layer constants in 30 files (for example Commands/RafterJoistCommands.cs 20-24, Services/TieDownService.cs 27, Services/TimberSubfloorService.cs 48-58, Services/FoundationService.cs 21-25). Colours and linetypes are taken by name from the office template drawing (LayerService.cs 540); the names themselves are not on the Settings page, except for the few groups that carry their own layer (roof and floor setout, lintels, level carry, framing legend, bored pier plan, basement, pump pit, reo bars, foundation plan, weld mark). Not a wrong number, but a wrong layer on paper is the risk: an object plotted with the wrong line weight or frozen with the wrong layer. Right result: one layer name per kind of object, held on the Settings page (proposed Layers.<Kind>, Layers tab, labels such as 'Layer for beams'), read by every command that draws that object, so a pier is on the same layer whichever command drew it. Smallest fix: first make the four double-ups agree (Tim to say which layer name is right for each), then move the layer map onto the Settings page. To SEE it: draw a bored pier with BP and another with the bored pier plan tool and check the layer of each in the Layer Properties palette (today: BORED PIER and BORED PIER UNDER); repeat with joists and a stump footing. ## BUG-536

**Command / Area:** R00_STRUC items 5, 7, 20, 23, 24, 26, 27 and 34 (MEDIUM; EIGHT commands that ignore a Settings name that already exists, or read it for only part of the job). What the drafter sees: they change a value on the Settings page (or in the file) and the command carries on with its own built-in number. The eight, all under Modules/Structural: (1) SCREWPILE: offers 300 (Services/FoundationScrewPileService.cs 172) while FootingWidth.ScrewPileDiameterMm is 150 (Models/UserSettings.cs 1115, fallback Services/FoundationService.cs 28), so a pile redrawn without a size is 150 and a new one is offered 300; the two numbers disagree. (2) BP (bored pier): offers [300/450/600] <450> (Services/FoundationService.cs 1981-1992) and ignores BoredPierPlan.DefaultDiameterMm = 450 (Models/UserSettings.cs 1567); always uses block 450DIABPV2 (2012-2013); the hatched version is offered only for 450 (1998). (3) REBAR / RB: starts at N12, 200 mm, 3 bars (Services/NativeTimToolsService.cs 31-35) and ignores Rebar.DefaultSize and Rebar.DefaultSpacing (N12 / 200, on the Settings page). (4) Beam shorten: the two choices 45 and 100 are fixed (Commands/BeamPlacementCommands.cs 1426-1437); only the last pick is remembered in Beams.LastShortenDistance (in the file only). (5) Every label command: Layouts.LabelPlotHeightMm is read by two commands of 25 (see BUG-531). (6) Member schedule (XCLMTXT / EXCELMTEXT): row and text sizes are built in at Services/ExcelMTextService.cs 37-53 and 4091-4094 (mark text 300, description 200, row 750, boxes 1450 and 4700 wide, column set 6950, bands 750); only Excel.RowsPerColumn 31, Excel.FloorSectionGap 3000 and the text offsets are on the page. They must match the office MEMBER SCHEDULE block. (7) Footing schedule: text 250, row 350, 1:100 when no scale is set (Services/ScheduleService.cs 36-38) and column widths 3600 and 1800 (Services/FoundationScheduleService.cs 32-33); the sizes follow Layouts.LabelPlotHeightMm but the widths do not follow any Settings value. (8) CSLOADPATH: Models/UserSettings.cs 1315-1321 holds LoadPath.AssumedPointLoadKN (20), .AssumedAllowableBearingKPa (100), .MinPadSizeMm (450) in the file only, and the round-up to the next 50 mm (Structural.DesignCore/LoadPathEngine.cs 214) and a pier with no size counted as 450 (LoadPathEngine.cs 141) are built in. A wrong number on paper is the risk: the drafter believes the Settings value is in force and the pile size, the pad offered or the schedule sizing on the sheet come from a different built-in number. Right result: each of the eight reads its Settings name (adding the missing names, for example Rebar.DefaultBarCount, Beams.ShortenChoicesMm, BoredPierPlan.DiameterChoicesMm, FootingSchedule.ColumnWidths, MemberSchedule.TextHeights, .RowHeight, .ColumnWidths, LoadPath.PadRoundUpMm), and the two pile numbers become one. Smallest fix: wire the existing names first (REBAR, BP, SCREWPILE), then add the missing names. To SEE it: change Rebar default size to N16 on CESETTINGS and run REBAR (today: still N12); change the bored pier plan diameter and run BP (today: still 450); run SCREWPILE and compare the offered size with the size drawn for a pile without one. ## BUG-538

**Command / Area:** R00_CIVIL items 4 (the council and rising-main parts), 5 and 6 (MEDIUM-HIGH; council rules written into the code, so a council change needs a new build of the plugin). What the drafter sees: CDDESIGN gives a storage or a pump result that follows rules the plugin carries inside itself, not the council profile and not the Settings page. If a council changes its rule, nothing changes until a new plugin build, and the drafter cannot see or correct the number. The values, each with file:line: (1) Bayside: the pump station storm is forced to 1 in 20 (Services/PumpSizingService.cs 125, applied at 303-306 as the audit gives it); (2) rising main size: 50 mm up to 5 L/s, otherwise 80 mm (Services/PumpSizingService.cs 98, 101, 104; the audit calls this an office habit, not a named council rule, and it has no Settings name); (3) Kingston: a 500 L credit for each 2000 L block of reuse (Services/ReuseCreditService.cs 31-34, 75, 78); (4) Manningham: a factor of 0.25, applying only with at least 2000 L of reuse and 50 m2 of roof (same file, same lines); (5) Casey: a reuse credit of one-third (same file); (6) Casey orifice formula constant K 21.9 (Services/OrificeSizer.cs 55, used by CDDESIGN at Services/AutoDesignService.cs 409 when the Casey profile has no orificeFormulaK; the council field exists, but the code keeps its own copy as the fallback; the audit marks this item 'partly'). The reuse credits reach the CDDESIGN storage result (Services/AutoDesignOrchestrator.cs 154) and the pump rules reach the CDDESIGN pump result (Services/AutoDesignOrchestrator.cs 173). The reuse rules are not in Assets/Config/council-profiles.json at all. A wrong council number on a design is the risk: a storage or a pump sized on an out-of-date council rule, with nothing on the sheet to show the number came from the plugin and not from the council. Right result: council rules live in the council profile / Settings page, each with the source and the edition named, so a council change is a Settings edit and not a new build (proposed council profile fields reuseCreditRule, reuseBlockL, reuseCreditPerBlockL, reuseFactor, reuseMinL, reuseMinRoofM2 shown on the council page under 'Rainwater reuse credit'; the Bayside 1 in 20 in the Bayside profile; the Casey K 21.9 in the Casey profile; the rising main split as Pump.RisingMainSplitLps, Pump.RisingMainSmallMm, Pump.RisingMainLargeMm). Where a profile has no value the program says 'Casey K not set' and carries on (R-12, R-27), never a quiet code copy. Smallest fix: move the Bayside 1 in 20 and the Casey 21.9 into their profiles and read them from there; then add the reuse fields and the rising main boxes. Tim's word is needed on each council source and edition (engineering judgement). To SEE it: look for the reuse credit, the Bayside storm and the Casey K on the council page (today none is there); run CDDESIGN on a copy of a Kingston job with reuse tank volume and note the credit it takes off the storage, then try to change the credit from Settings (today it cannot be changed without a new build). ## BUG-543

**Command / Area:** R00_CIVIL items 2 and 24 (MEDIUM; the CDCALC Detention System tab always sizes the orifice with 0.6, and two other tabs use 0.61). What the drafter sees: the orifice hole worked out in the CDCALC Detention System tab always uses a coefficient of 0.6 and gravity 9.81. CDDESIGN draws with the coefficient in the council profile (the orificeCo field, the same field CDRULES shows) and gravity 9.8. All 22 council profiles in Assets/Config/council-profiles.json hold 0.6 today, so the holes agree today. Change one council profile and the two screens give different holes, and nothing tells the drafter. Evidence: ViewModels/DetentionSystemViewModel.cs 16-17 (the 0.6 and the 9.81), used at 892, 1014 and 1034; CDDESIGN reads the profile at Services/AutoDesignService.cs 454-456, CDRULES at Rules/RulebookValues.cs 250, and gravity 9.8 sits at Services/Hydraulics.cs 33. Item 24: the Orifice calc tab (ViewModels/OrificeCalcViewModel.cs 18) and the Detention Design tab (ViewModels/DetentionDesignViewModel.cs 25) start at 0.61, so the audit finds 0.6, 0.61 and the council field in use at once, and gravity 9.8 against 9.81 (two of the audit's seven disagreement cases). I think the gravity difference moves the hole by about a quarter of a per cent; I have not run it. The audit marks the orifice coefficient as a standards value to cite. Right result: every screen reads the one rulebook coefficient (the council field), the office figure used when the council gives none is a Settings value (proposed Detention.OfficeOrificeCo, Detention and orifices tab, 'Orifice coefficient used when the council gives none'), and gravity is one figure for every screen (not a Settings value). The source of 0.6 is cited. Smallest fix: make the Detention System, Orifice calc and Detention Design tabs read the same coefficient as CDRULES, and use one gravity. To SEE it: on a copy of a job, change the council profile orificeCo to a figure other than 0.6 and compare the hole in CDCALC Detention System with the hole CDDESIGN draws (today they differ; right: the same). **Command / Area:** R00_CIVIL items 19 and 20 (MEDIUM-HIGH, ENGINEERING-RESULT RISK; two or three Settings names for one thing, two of the audit's top 40 and the only ones the audit marks 'several names'). What the drafter sees: they edit the one value they can find and some commands move while others do not. (1) Detention freeboard has two Settings names and a built-in: Pipe.DetentionFreeboardMm (Models/UserSettings.cs 506, read by CDTWL at Services/DetentionTwlService.cs 363) and DesignStandards.DetentionFreeboardMm (Models/UserSettings.cs 1375, read by CDRULES at Rules/RulebookValues.cs 237), plus a built-in 150 at Rules/DetentionTwlSolver.cs 109. (2) The pit drop has three Settings names and a built-in: Inverts.PitInvertDropMm (Models/UserSettings.cs 631), Inverts.MinOutletDropMm (614, the only one with a box on the page) and DesignStandards.PitInvertDropMm (1365), plus Rules/RulebookSettings.cs 46 (20). All are 20 today. I did not trace which screen reads which (the audit does not either), so which command follows the box on the page is not known. A wrong number on a design or on paper is the risk: a top water level or a pit invert drop that the drafter changed in the box and that CDTWL, CD or CDRULES then ignore, or read from a different name, giving a different level on the drawing and on the check. Right result: one name, one box for each (proposed: Detention and orifices tab, 'Freeboard below the lid (mm)'; Pipes tab, 'Drop across a pit (mm)'), read everywhere, and the two or three old names removed or made to point at the one. ## BUG-550

**Command / Area:** OFF-PC CALLS AUDIT routes 1, 2 and 3 (HIGH; BLOCKS COLLEAGUE INSTALL with gate item 10; same family and same fix as BUG-549, which named only CEMARKUP; this entry lists EVERY route in the markup / AI family so none is missed). Structural CEMARKUPBENCH, CEMARKUPPARSE, the CEMARKUP window's Parse button and CEMARKUP 'Ask AI' send job data to OpenAI, not Claude. (a) CEMARKUPBENCH uploads every PDF in a folder AND all its subfolders: Modules/Structural/Commands/MarkupAICommands.cs 304-383 (folder search is SearchOption.AllDirectories, line 347; default source mode Hybrid includes the upload, 339-344; default folder is the last markup folder or the Markups folder); upload in Services/MarkupAIVisionParser.cs 106-131 (POST files, purpose=user_data) then 133-179 (POST responses). Each whole PDF goes as bytes with its file name and a short prompt 'ProjectType=STR...'; nothing is blanked. OpenAI KEEPS every file because the code has no delete call (no HttpMethod.Delete anywhere in Structural). The command is listed, not hidden, in Assets/Config/command-registry.json 671. (b) CEMARKUPPARSE: MarkupAICommands.cs 53-88 then Services/MarkupAIWorkflowService.cs 39-62 then MarkupAIOrchestratorService.cs 64-66 then MarkupAIVisionParser.Parse. The whole PDF, its file name and the drawing type go to OpenAI when the drafter presses Enter at 'Source mode [Bluebeam/Hand/hYbrid] <Hybrid>'; only 'Bluebeam' avoids the upload; MarkupParseRequest.UseVisionParser also defaults to true (Models/MarkupAIModels.cs 64). The raw OpenAI reply is saved next to the package (MarkupAIWorkflowService.cs 78-83). (c) The CEMARKUP window's Parse button: UI/Palette/MarkupAIPanel.xaml.cs 143-146, the source combo defaults to Hybrid (MarkupAIPanel.xaml 48); same path as (b). (d) CEMARKUP 'Ask AI' chat: UI/Palette/MarkupAIPanel.xaml.cs 280-295 then Services/MarkupAIChatService.cs 32-83 (POST responses), payload built at 200-244. It sends the typed question, the package ID, the project code (worked out from the drawing name), the FULL DRAWING PATH (drawing = package.BaseDrawingPath, line 237; normally holds the Windows login and the client or job folder, for example C:\Users\<login>\OneDrive - ...\Projects\<job>), each markup item's text, layer and command, and up to 10 unresolved items with their raw text. The 'Enable chat' switch (MarkupAI.ChatEnabled) is honoured but DEFAULTS ON (MarkupAIModels.cs 238). THE SWITCH THAT DOES NOTHING: 'Enable MarkupAI' (MarkupAI.Enabled, default ON, MarkupAIModels.cs 224) is shown in CE Settings but is read by NOTHING before an upload, so a drafter who unticks it still uploads. The 'Share learning data' switch (MarkupAI.LearningDataOptIn, default ON) is also read by nothing; no data is shared by it but the label misleads. KEY AND ADDRESS: the key comes from the environment variable named in Settings (MarkupAI.OpenAiApiKeyEnvVar, default OPENAI_API_KEY, MarkupAIVisionParser.cs 45), never from a file; the web address is MarkupAI.OpenAiBaseUrl from the settings file (default https://api.openai.com/v1, MarkupAIModels.cs 227), so editing that file could send the key and the PDFs to any address. If no key is set, the commands skip and say 'Set environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY'. WHAT A DRAFTER SEES: nothing. No warning, no question, no tick-box: the PDF is simply uploaded when the drafter presses Enter at the Hybrid prompt, and the chat sends the job folder path on the button. On a job: a markup PDF carrying the client name and the site address sits on OpenAI's servers with no way for CE to remove it. TIM'S RULE, VERIFIED IN HIS OWN WORDS (UX-QA-05, 25/26 Sep): 'Yes, Claude only, page only (Recommended)': only the markup PAGE image goes, only to CLAUDE through CE's own connection (never OpenAI), never kept for training, with the title-block area blanked; and when the title block cannot be blanked, 'Don't send; say so (Recommended)': CE does not send that page and tells the user to tag that page's marks by hand. Sources: decisions\2026-09-25_V3_PLAN_DISCUSSION_RULINGS.md line 772 and 04_REFERENCE\structural\cards\STRUC-MARKUP-QA_CARD_2026-09-26.md lines 74-75 and 90. These routes break all three parts. TIM'S PC: no OPENAI_API_KEY is set in any scope (read by controller 06, see BUG-549), so nothing leaves today. A colleague PC with that variable set WOULD upload; the audit did not read any colleague PC. RIGHT RESULT AND SMALLEST FIX (audit fixes 1 and 2, for Tim to rule on): nothing leaves the PC unless a Settings value that DEFAULTS OFF is on. Make CEMARKUP read MarkupAI.Enabled before ANY upload and default it OFF (and ChatEnabled OFF) until the Claude route exists; or hide CEMARKUPPARSE, CEMARKUPBENCH and the Parse and Ask AI buttons for colleagues. When on: one page at a time, to Claude only, title block blanked or the page not sent; the chat never sends the drawing path; delete any provider-side copy; refuse a web address that is not the approved one. HOW TO SEE IT IN AUTOCAD: on a PC with a TEST key set, run CEMARKUPPARSE on a one-page PDF and press Enter at the Hybrid prompt: right = a plain message that markup AI is off and nothing sent (check the network or the provider's file list shows nothing new); CEMARKUPBENCH says off; the Parse button and Ask AI say off; Settings shows both switches OFF and unticking or ticking them changes the result. LINKS: BUG-549 (same family, same fix; this entry widens it), BUG-551 (Civil AI paths), gate item 10 in areas/release-v3-colleagues.md. It does NOT limit pages, does NOT inspect images or PDFs and does NOT blank a title block. ## BUG-552

**Command / Area:** OFF-PC CALLS AUDIT routes 9, 10 and 11 (MEDIUM-HIGH; the 'office folder, coded' rule is broken in THREE places). The rule, as the audit states it (not Tim's exact words): support zips and fault reports never leave the PC except into the office IT folder, and only coded (no real login, PC name or job names). (a) Civil fault reports reach the office IT folder UNCODED: Modules/Manager/Plugin.cs 137-152 (start-up plus 15 seconds) and Commands/PluginManagerCommands.cs 116 (CEMANAGERREFRESH) copy module telemetry through Services/CeAdminStorageService.cs 122-135 into <IT Admin>\CE Plugin Admin\. In Civil's records the drawing file name is in clear (Modules/Drainage/Services/AdminTelemetryService.cs 324 and 403) and the fault details are the raw error text (Details = ex.ToString(), line 176), which can hold full paths with the login and the client folder. Structural scrubs both (Modules/Structural/Services/AdminTelemetryService.cs 198-209, 428). SECOND PROBLEM in the same route: Civil and Structural write to %APPDATA%\TIM_CE_CADTOOLS\CE_Admin\outbox (Shared/CE_SHARED/Services/CeTelemetryStore.cs 60-68) but the Manager uploads from %APPDATA%\CE_CADTOOLS\CE_Admin\outbox and moves the old folder across only once, when the new one does not exist yet (CeAdminStorageService.cs 25-43). So Civil and Structural records probably reach the office folder only once, at that first move: a working-order problem as well as a privacy one (the audit did not check the real start-up order on a colleague PC). (b) CEMANAGERDIAG report has a coded file name but the REAL LOGIN INSIDE: Modules/Manager/Services/CeDiagnosticsService.cs 300-311 writes <IT Admin>\CE Diagnostics\<coded PC>\<time>_<coded login>.txt (or Desktop\CE Diagnostics when the IT folder is missing); the body carries the full IT Admin path, the OneDriveCommercial path and every loaded DLL path (96-101, 236), which normally include C:\Users\<login>. The body is not run through the scrubber. (c) Support zips are saved to the DESKTOP: Manager CESUPPORT, Services/CeSupportBundleService.cs 49-56 (Desktop\CE Diagnostics; contents scrubbed of login and PC name); Structural Services/SupportBundleService.cs 33-34 (Desktop\CE_Support_<time>.zip; logs and failures). CE uploads nothing itself, but company PCs often back the Desktop up to OneDrive, so the zip, with logs that name drawings and jobs, would sync into the person's own OneDrive and not the IT folder. The audit did not check any colleague's Desktop. WHAT A DRAFTER / COLLEAGUE SEES: nothing; they press 'Send a fault report' or run CESUPPORT / CEMANAGERDIAG and a file appears. On a job: the office IT folder (and, for the Desktop zips, possibly a personal OneDrive) holds files naming the real login and client job folders. RIGHT RESULT AND SMALLEST FIX (audit fixes 4 and 5, for Tim to rule on): run Civil's fault Message and Details through the same scrubber Structural uses; scrub the CEMANAGERDIAG report body (paths coded, no real login); save support zips to a local AppData folder first, then copy into the IT folder, coded; fix the two outbox folder names so they match. HOW TO SEE IT IN AUTOCAD: cause a Civil fault, run CEMANAGERREFRESH, open the new file in the IT folder: right = no real login, PC name, drawing name or client folder in it. Run CEMANAGERDIAG and search the report text for your Windows login: right = not found. Run CESUPPORT: right = the zip lands in an AppData folder or the IT folder, not the Desktop. LINKS (same family, some overlap, filed earlier from Audit 01): BUG-488 (CEMANAGERDIAG and the fault-report button write the real login, PC name and user folder: this audit's route 10 is the same fault), BUG-489 (CESUPPORT zip cleaner misses drawing names and paths), BUG-491 (A6 Manager failure reports, A7 Civil failure text not scrubbed and the same one-time move, A10 Structural's old support zip said to be dormant in 1.0.110). New here: the Desktop-syncs-to-OneDrive point and the Structural Desktop zip path in 1.0.112 (the audit names a 'diagnostics command'; BUG-491 A10 said no command reached it in 1.0.110, so whether it is reachable now is not established). Structural writes real drawing names into the plugins' upload folder (usage records: Structural telemetry lines 364 and 428; machine report line 307), a HIGH when the #954 fault-record upload switch is ON (the default OFF touches nothing, so nothing leaks in any waiting payload today). #954 @ 0e51479e is MERGE-WITH-FIXES and stays out: upload ONLY Civil-marked records and delete the rest; the plugins' fault text goes through #941's path cutter (MEDIUM: fault records keep drawing and job-folder paths).
